clue.text: The case for the prosecution

parts.note: reads as the argument a prosecutor brings in court, but 'case' is the grammatical one: the noun case used when blaming or charging someone, in a pun on accusing

explanation.surface: A lawyer outlines the argument against the defendant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks legal, but it is a grammatical case; the one named after accusing suits the prosecution.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, the case marking a verb's direct object takes its Latin name from accusing, the prosecutor's job.

clue.text: A French cleric born in Lincoln

indicators.note: the letter for born goes inside the name for Lincoln

parts.note: Abe is US President Abraham Lincoln

explanation.surface: A French priest whose birthplace was Lincoln in England.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln looks like the English city but is the president, ABE.
explanation.definitionFit: The French title for a priest or churchman, used for clergy without a parish.

clue.text: King, queen, jack or jester

parts.note: lists playing cards with faces; the jester stands for the joker in a pack

explanation.surface: A list of royal household figures and the court fool.
explanation.walkthrough: The jester is the joker of a pack; with the royals it suggests a palace court, which is the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The picture cards of a playing-card pack, named for the royal court they depict.

clue.text: So modern in retrospect was this city of iniquity

indicators.note: looking back, the word for modern is read backwards

explanation.surface: Was the wicked biblical city so up to date, looking back?
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical city destroyed by God for its wickedness, alongside Gomorrah.

clue.text: Attempt to include one account of a play-cycle

indicators.note: the word for attempt takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a try is an attempt
I is the Roman numeral one
a log is a record or account

explanation.surface: Someone tries to write a history of a theatrical series.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of three connected works, such as Aeschylus's Oresteia.

clue.text: He calls for it to be set in the sun-screen

indicators.note: the word it is placed inside the word for the sun-screen

parts.note: a visor shades the eyes from the sun

explanation.surface: Someone asks for something to be fitted into a sunshade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calls' means pays a visit, not shouts or telephones.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest who pays a call on someone, dropping in to see them.

clue.text: In a superior position at work

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone sits above colleagues in the office.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on top of something places it higher up, in an elevated spot.

clue.text: A hearing problem

definitions.meaning: a court case heard before a judge
a trouble or ordeal, as in ... and tribulations

explanation.surface: Someone has trouble with their ears.
explanation.definitionFit: A court case examined before a judge, and also a test of endurance or a hardship.

clue.text: More than fair description of the attractive and virtuous

parts.note: pretty means attractive
good means virtuous

explanation.surface: A phrase describing people both handsome and upright.
explanation.definitionFit: Quite satisfactory, better than middling.

clue.text: Start playing golf now that the whist championship is cancelled

parts.note: a whist drive is a card tournament
off means called off, cancelled

explanation.surface: A card player goes to the links since the tournament was scrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: A whist drive is a social card-playing competition, popular in British village halls.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers begin a hole by striking from the tee, the opening shot.

clue.text: Spring is on the way

definitions.meaning: to spring is to leap forward
heading somewhere, as in a train for London

explanation.surface: The new season is approaching.
explanation.definitionFit: A leap is a jump, and a traveller headed for a place is said to be bound for it.

clue.text: Used to be a domestic

parts.note: describes someone who once worked as a household servant; phrased like a past tense, the definition is the state of being employed in a household

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a former life as a maid.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a verb phrase, but the answer is the phrase describing a servant's employment.
explanation.definitionFit: Maids and butlers were employed in a house, working for a family as staff.

clue.text: Get rid of a politician with a corpulent frame

indicators.note: the fat man's frame goes around the rest, so this word signals one piece wrapping the others

parts.note: corpulent means stout, fat
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Voters eject an overweight member of parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: To crush or eliminate something completely, as with a fire or a rebellion, is to destroy it.

clue.text: Gentleman's gentleman writes a very unusual tale

indicators.note: the letters of the word tale are given in an unusual, rearranged order

explanation.surface: A butler turns author and writes an odd story.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentleman's personal manservant is traditionally called his gentleman, Jeeves being the classic example.

clue.text: Dressing a boy in Sunday best

indicators.note: a boy goes inside the letters for Sunday and best

parts.note: the cream is the best part
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Dressing a child in their finest church clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Dressing looks like a verb about clothes but is the noun: a condiment for lettuce. It is a British bottled mayonnaise-like sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: A creamy condiment poured on lettuce, popular in Britain.

clue.text: Fervent admission of a Conservative

parts.note: an admission is a confession, here the 'am' of 'I am'
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Someone passionately declares allegiance to the Conservative Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I am a Tory' is the admission; the solver drops the I and keeps the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Passionate, ardent, in the romantic sense of love-making.

clue.text: Lose credit as the result of running a lottery

parts.note: when a race has been run it is over, finished
a draw is a lottery or raffle

explanation.surface: Someone goes into debt from running a raffle.
explanation.definitionFit: To take more money from a bank account than it holds, going into the red.

clue.text: Getting firmly established is cheering

definitions.meaning: a plant sending down roots settles in
fans shouting support for a team

explanation.surface: A supporter's enthusiasm becomes a fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants anchor themselves by growing roots, and American fans root for their team when they shout encouragement.

clue.text: Fighting with energy, but having difficulty

parts.note: someone in a scrap is in a fight
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Battling energetically while struggling.
explanation.definitionFit: In trouble or a predicament, an idiom for a tight spot.

clue.text: Lecture on clothing of the Christian era

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks years of the Christian era
dress means clothing

explanation.surface: A talk about what people wore in early Christian times.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal speech or talk given to an audience.

clue.text: Joins up with one leaving the army

indicators.note: the letter for one departs from the word for the army

parts.note: soldiers make up the army
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone enlists while another quits the forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuses metal pieces together with melted alloy.

clue.text: Enthusiast has a look for cattle

parts.note: a buff is a keen fan, as in a film buff
lo is an old word meaning look, behold

explanation.surface: A fan takes a look at some cows.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffalo is a large wild ox, a kind of bovine.

clue.text: A sore spot for the British in venter of the antiseptic system

parts.words: in venter of the antiseptic system
parts.note: the page splits 'inventor'; Joseph Lister pioneered antiseptic surgery

explanation.surface: A sore spot for the British in the history of antiseptic medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'in venter', a split of 'inventor'. Joseph Lister was the British surgeon who introduced antiseptic methods.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised bubble of skin filled with fluid, a painful patch.

clue.text: Had the ability to be fashionable in chilly weather

indicators.note: the fashionable letter goes inside the word for chilly weather

parts.note: cold weather is chilly
U means upper-class, socially acceptable

explanation.surface: Someone manages to look stylish in the cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of can: was able to.

clue.text: Some Beirut terrorists are to make pronouncement

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Militants in Lebanon intend to issue a statement.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak or say something aloud, voicing a statement.

clue.text: Relaxed in a reclining chair

definitions.meaning: literally lying with the back tilted down

explanation.surface: Someone takes it easy in a recliner.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy-going people are described with this phrase, which also literally pictures someone lying with their back lowered.

clue.text: I go into an agricultural storehouse — a little one in Scotland

indicators.note: the letter I enters the farm building

parts.note: a barn stores crops on a farm

explanation.surface: Someone enters a farm building, where a Scottish child waits.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots word for a child.

clue.text: The most faithful friend Lear had in England

definitions.text: The most faithful friend Lear had
definitions.meaning: the Earl of ... stays loyal to King Lear in Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: King Lear's truest companion was English.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's loyal earl in King Lear shares his name with the south-eastern English county, the Garden of England.

clue.text: He is sociable, but exception ally green

parts.note: the page splits 'exceptionally', and extra as an adverb means exceptionally, as in extra large
vert is heraldic green

explanation.surface: A friendly man who is unusually inexperienced.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'exception ally', a split of 'exceptionally'. 'Green' looks like naive but is the heraldic colour VERT.
explanation.definitionFit: An outgoing, gregarious person, the opposite of an introvert; this is an older spelling.

clue.text: I make harsh criticisms when in a rage

parts.note: to rate someone is an old verb meaning to scold them severely

explanation.surface: Someone admits to scolding people when furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Furious, very angry.

clue.text: He was saintly to a greater extent

definitions.meaning: Sir Thomas ..., the Tudor statesman, was canonised as a saint

explanation.surface: A man's holiness exceeded expectations.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More was made a saint in 1935, and the word also means additionally or to a larger degree.

clue.text: Severe strain breaks a man

indicators.note: the word strain breaks up and its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a gent is a man

explanation.surface: Heavy stress causes a man to break down.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh or sharply critical, as an acid tongue or a stern remark.
